# Backup sidecar: pg_dump, Qdrant snapshot HTTP, media tar, age, scheduled via supercronic.
FROM alpine:3.22

RUN apk add --no-cache \
	age \
	bash \
	ca-certificates \
	coreutils \
	curl \
	findutils \
	jq \
	postgresql17-client \
	supercronic \
	tar \
	tzdata

COPY common.sh backup.sh restore.sh entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/
RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/backup.sh /usr/local/bin/restore.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh \
	&& chmod 644 /usr/local/bin/common.sh

# /media is the shared media_data volume. Docker seeds a named volume's root
# ownership from the image directory of whichever container mounts it first, and
# this service reaches `healthy` deps long before the backend does (which waits
# for the ml-service model download). Without this directory the volume would be
# created root-owned and the backend, running as uid 1000, could not write to it.
RUN mkdir -p /media && chown 1000:1000 /media

WORKDIR /backups
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]
=== BACKUP.md head ===
# Online backups (Postgres, Qdrant, media)

DaZ-Pilot writes three persistent stores. This sidecar backs them up **without stopping** the API, worker, dashboard, or ML service.

| Store            | How                                                      | Runtime impact                                               |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| PostgreSQL       | `pg_dump -Fc` (transaction snapshot)                     | None. Writers continue.                                      |
| Qdrant           | One snapshot per collection via HTTP, plus the alias map | None (hot snapshots).                                        |
| `media_data`     | `tar` of the live volume                                 | Files written _during_ the tar may be missing or incomplete. |
| `ml_model_cache` | Not backed up                                            | Re-downloaded from Hugging Face.                             |

**Why per-collection and not a full storage snapshot:** Qdrant can _create_ a full storage snapshot over HTTP, but it can only _restore_ one through the CLI at startup (`qdrant --storage-snapshot ...`). Only collection snapshots have a recover endpoint. Per-collection snapshots therefore keep restore possible against the running Qdrant of this stack. The alias map (`school_<uuid>` → `school_<uuid>__v<timestamp>`) is captured separately from `GET /aliases`, since collection snapshots do not carry aliases.

There is **no distributed freeze** across the three stores. Dump, Qdrant snapshot, and tar run one after another, so a few seconds to minutes of cross-store drift is possible (e.g. ingest finished in Qdrant before Postgres recorded the job). Account and learning data live in Postgres; ML drift is repairable by re-ingest/training. **Do not mix artifacts from different sets** on restore.

Restore **does** require a maintenance window. See [RESTORE.md](RESTORE.md).

The only interface is **Docker Compose**. Coolify (or any other wrapper) just runs this file; there are no Coolify-specific scripts.

## Starting it

The `backup` service is part of the stack, so it starts with everything else:

```sh
docker compose up -d --build
```

It then runs on `BACKUP_SCHEDULE` (default 03:00 UTC) inside the container. Coolify needs no special handling — it deploys this same file.

**It refuses to start without `AGE_RECIPIENT`** (see below). That is deliberate: a misconfigured key should surface at deploy time, not at 03:00. Check with `docker compose logs backup`.

Manual run, any time, alongside the scheduler:

```sh
docker compose run --rm backup backup.sh
```

The hot-reload dev stack (`-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml`) excludes the service via profile `ops`; add `--profile ops` there if you want to exercise it locally.

## Encryption

Backups are encrypted with [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age). Generate a key pair on a trusted machine (not necessarily the app host):

```sh
age-keygen -o age-identity.txt
# public key is printed and stored in the file as `# public key: age1...`
```

Put the **public** key in `.env` as `AGE_RECIPIENT`. Keep `age-identity.txt` **off the app server** if you can; you only need it for restore. Never commit the identity.

Several recipients: comma-separated `AGE_RECIPIENT`.

Local drills without keys (plaintext, throwaway data only):

```env
BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=true
```

Without `AGE_RECIPIENT` and without that flag, the container exits on start and `backup.sh` refuses to run.
